newsitem.title: USA: Democrats name six to U.S. House Ag Committee.
newsitem.headline: Democrats name six to U.S. House Ag Committee.

text.p: Democrats named six newcomers to serve on the U.S. House Agricutlure Committee, including Marion Barry of Arkansas, the former White House farm adviser.
Also named were Virgil Goode of Virginia, Mike McIntyre of North Carolina, Debbie Stabenow of Michigan, Bob Ethridge of North Carolina and Chris John of Louisiana.

In addition, two Democrats won plum assignments that took them off the Agriculture Committee. Karen Thurman of Florida was given a seat on the Ways and Means Committee and Ed Pastor of Arizona was assigned to the Appropriations Committee.
Appropriations and Ways and Means are two "exclusive" committees whose members are not allowed to hold other posts.
All told, six Democrats would leave the committee. Four retired, were defeated or were elected to the Senate.
The approach taken by Democrats allowed for possible changes in the ratio of Republicans and Democrats, now 27-22, to reflect inroads by Democrats into Republican control of the House.
